questions.q: Why does a template change need staged rollout discipline that a single-repo pipeline change doesn't?
options: Templates cannot be tagged with semantic versions
GitHub forbids more than one repo from referencing the same tag
Staged rollout removes the need for a changelog
A bad release can break every one of the hundreds of repos that move onto it at once, instead of just one
questions.explain: Because so many repos depend on the same template, a bad version can break all of them simultaneously unless the rollout is deliberately staged.

questions.q: In the ring-based rollout described in this lesson, what has to happen before Ring 1 (early adopters) moves onto the new version?
options: Ring 2 (general availability) must already be complete
Ring 0's canary repos must have run clean for a full day of normal traffic
The old v1 tag must be deleted from the repository
A support ticket must be filed by every team in the organization
questions.explain: Early adopters only move once the canary ring has demonstrated a clean run under normal traffic, which is the gate between rings.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say build/test duration matters during a canary, even when every job reports success?
options: Duration has no effect on whether a canary is considered healthy
Longer builds automatically fail the required status check
A change that quietly doubles CI time is still a real regression, even when the pipeline goes green
Canary repos are not allowed to take longer than one minute to build
questions.explain: A passing pipeline that now takes far longer is still a meaningful regression worth catching during the canary window, not just outright failures.

questions.q: What is the correct response when a canary repo shows a bad signal during the rollout window?
options: Stop widening, fix the template, cut a new beta tag, and re-run the canary
Proceed to Ring 1 while continuing to investigate the issue
Immediately re-point the moving v1 tag at the new version anyway
Delete the canary repo so the signal stops appearing
questions.explain: A bad canary signal should halt further widening until the template is fixed and re-validated, not be worked around while the rollout continues.

questions.q: What problem does a version-bump bot like Renovate or Dependabot solve during a template rollout?
options: It automatically rewrites the template's own source code
It opens an automated, reviewable pull request per repo to bump the pinned tag, instead of a human hand-editing hundreds of files
It removes the need for a canary ring entirely
It merges every pull request without any human review
questions.explain: The bot turns a manual, error-prone edit across hundreds of repos into individually reviewable, individually revertible pull requests.
